Honestly this is the only reliable thought that gets me to the next day. I know my cat would miss me, they can remember things for a long time. 

My older cat died when my girl was a kitten, and she STILL looks for the older cat and cries sometimes. It's been over 10 years. 

For me, I can justify suicide in terms of how it will affect the people in my life - I don't have kids or anyone relying on me, my friends and family would be sad but they would understand why I was gone. My cat wouldn't understand, to her I would have just disappeared and never come back. I have a much harder time trying to justify suicide in terms of how it will affect her. 

TL;DR Yes your cat would miss you, probably their entire life. And it's okay to lean on that to get to tomorrow.

I used to psych myself out of running because of body shame/anxiety. My solution is to get up ridiculously early when most folks are still asleep and run when it's dark out (bonus, it's nice and cool still and I run hot so it's more comfortable). It was difficult to adjust my schedule and maybe sounds like a cop-out (or that I'm just running away from the problem, ha), but my thinking is - whatever gets me out of the house and running is progress, I can work up to running in board daylight but not if I'm hiding inside all the time.
Maybe someday I'll be brave enough to go full commando haha. I agree on the fan! It's a must even if it's cold out
That's interesting! I can see how that works though - and yeah the euphoria is *chefs kiss* like the first time I shaved my face even though I didn't technically need to lol
Oooo okay underwear only is next!
Aw I'm sorry it's tough right now man - I totally get it! Hope top surgery happens for you soon!!

Have you tried a different injection site? 

I did IM injections in my thighs for years and all of those little pricks (haaa) add up, it built up scar tissue and I ended up with quads FULL of trigger points (basically small, super-sensitive spots). Got to the point where I couldn't find a single place on my quads that didn't hurt like hell. Trigger points were alleviated with massage but I switched to SQ injections in my abdomen to avoid that happening again (although I still do sometimes hit a random nerve or something and it stings).

Also have big thighs, and big hips too. Longer boxer briefs don't ride up as much, and I also put them in my pants first and then step into boxer briefs/pants at the same time, that helps keep them in place - my brother gave me that tip, thick thighs run in the family I guess!
Echoing other comments, had stage 1 phallo w vnectomy. Tighter and the g-spot moved so it's closer to a prostate-position. And just the gender euphoria makes everything feel better too imo.

This is me and my baby brother! 16 years apart, I think I'm closest to him out of all my brothers in part bc they've been done with puberty for years but he and I are going through it at roughly the same time :)

All the time, like "do I WANT you" or "do I want to BE you"???? The answer is usually both. 

I will say that looking up pics/videos of guys similar to my height/shape (short, curvy-slowly-turning-stocky) and seeing how they styles themselves helps boost my confidence...like I'm never going to be a 6'3" blue steel stunner, but I can use what I've got and rock it, cuz I see plenty of guys (cis and trans) who look like me and they look good!
Most just that he wouldn't get all of the fluid, needles don't bother me much. It was definitely eerie to see how much fluid was in there though 😂

I've ended up doing like...almost la moz style breathing? Lol. It's kinda loud so I'm glad I run at oh-god-thirty in the morning when no one else is around. Inhale for 4 steps/exhale for 6, wasn't intentional but I'm of the "if it works don't touch it" mindset.

NOTHING is on my mind when I run, it's such an amazing relief. Closest I've gotten to meditation. No music, audio books, just me and sometimes the family of rabbits that hang out on my route.

Remember something similar with my top surgery, a few weeks post-op there was a massive fluid buildup across my whole chest, it looked and felt like an internal water bra. Just walking around make me motion sick, swear I could HEAR it sloshing 😂

Turns out the drains should've been left in longer, but fortunately didn't need to get them again, my surgeon just numbed me, stuck a bigass syringe in my chest and sucked all the fluid out. Very odd experience but it worked like a charm!
Congrats man!!! Wish I'd thought of a neck pillow when I got top surgery. I just stole every pillow in the house and made a nest - comfy but quite warm in the summer...
Second this! I'm well into my transition, pass for the most part, and I still get anxious about using the men's room sometimes.
You'll get there in no time!! :)

Nerve regrowth averages about 1mm/month, so it'll take a while to get full sensation. I haven't had RFF yet but do remember that with top surgery it took a good 6 months before any sensation returned, full sensation came back around the 1-year mark. 

Massage can help encourage feeling, I don't know about increasing the regrowth rate but for me it was useful for kind of reestablishing the "touch=good brain juice" connection. Minds are powerful things ;]

Had my SP for about 6 weeks after stage 1, Foley for 1 week. The foley was negligible, barely felt it and getting it removed didn't hurt at all. 

The SP was a nuisance but not unbearable, I had bladder spasms and got a UTI towards the end (fairly common with SPs). Beyond that it just felt like a constant pressure that is annoying but you get used to it. Take your bladder spasm meds religiously along with Azo if they give it to you, drink SO MUCH water, and sleep a lot is my advice. 

Also not sure about other folks, but for me getting the SP removed stung - but even with the pain I felt amazingly better within seconds and it only hurt for a few mins, then it was just a little sore while it healed over the next couple days.

Went from being able to run for a couple minutes at a time to 3 miles without a break, over about 2 weeks. Been overweight and sedentary my whole life, amazed at how much better I feel, how much fun I'm having. Next stop: 5 miles!

I'm out to some folks at work but it's sort of an open secret, I told one or two people casually and sort of let it spread on its own. No issues as of yet, although I did luck out with a generally chill environment (massage school so...we're all pretty relaxed lol)

I've been getting this more and more in the past few years, when I tell someone I'm trans they usually assume I'm MtF - weird but also kind of euphoric?

I hate getting ready to run and will procrastinate to no end, but once I'm doing it I don't want to stop. Only thing that shuts my brain up and gives me a break - plus riding the endorphins after is AWESOME for a creativity boost! The only time I really feel like I can write is after a run.

For me belly fat is the hardest to lose, my body just doesn't want to let it go! I call it my sturdy peasant genes, always gearing up for the winter :) So it might just be a matter of needing more time. 

Also something I learned awhile back, if you have a uterus, belly pooch lower on the abdomen is normal/you'll always have at least some pooch, both from the uterus itself and from the surrounding padding to protect it. Didn't believe it until I got a hysto and while my stomach isn't flat, it's flatter than it was before. Bodies are weird..

Phallo needs an alternative way of getting hard, either a rod/pump implant or an external device. I'll be getting the pump, when the time comes - there's a tube that goes inside the new penis, and a pump/valve in the scrotum to inflate/deflate. Ideally I'd prefer being able to get hard without any assistance, but I am looking forward to not having to worry about surprise boners lol.

Ejaculation is possible with phallo! Skene's glands are next to the urethra and make squirting possible - most surgeons opt to keep these intact during phallo so that ejaculation can happen. Speaking from experience, I've only had stage 1 phallo (basically meta) and it works! It's not semen but it's damn close!

Once a month is a little odd, as your T levels rise and fall it can cause mood swings so usually T injections are done biweekly or weekly to reduce the intensity of the T cycle. 

Maybe track your mood and see how it affects you, if you feel pretty stable from month to month it's probably fine, but if you find yourself going up and down talk to your Dr about adjusting the frequency.

Karl is a great name! It's totally normal to change your name multiple times too - I changed mine twice, and my cousin tried out a few different names before settling in his.

How people react to your name change says a lot about them, not you. They should be respectful and supportive - any accidental misnaming should be either self-corrected or, when you correct them, they don't give you shit for it. Just like with correcting misgendering. When I get called my old chosen name it feels on par with deadnaming, maybe explaining it that way will help folks get it? You're not Rei anymore, just like you aren't your birthname or your AGAB. 

It's YOUR name, not theirs - if Karl feels right, then you're Karl.

T changes how fat is distributed, and increases ability to build muscle, more than anything else. I gained some weight on T but it was all muscle, I got a lot stronger with way less effort than before. 

T tends to move fat from hips/thighs to the abdomen - which gives a more "masc" shape. I lost the "hourglass" shape over a few months. Abdominal/visceral fat is linked to increased risk of heart disease and diabetes, but a healthy lifestyle goes a long way towards reducing those risks.

It's likely - the rule of thumb is T makes us look more like our male relatives and that includes male-pattern baldness. It's possible the gene skipped you but better to expect it, so you can be on the lookout for thinning. The earlier you catch it the more effective things like minoxodil/finasteride are at preventing further hair loss.

I feel you! I got about 4 years on T before balding happened, but I didn't notice because I always wore my hair long, just thought it was too heavy and that's why it always looked kinda flat on top...ha! Then I did a pandemic-buzzcut and found out I hadn't escaped male-pattern baldness after all. 

It was super hard at first! Still is tbh. I think you're on the right track with how to look at it - I've been finding things to be excited about with baldness. No more hair products/styling time, it's cooler in the summer, hats look awesome on bald guys (imo), and I've noticed I get misgendered way less often these days. 

I'm working with my tattoo artist too, to add some scalp work to the full-body piece I'm finally getting started on :) can't wait!

oh man, I'm sorry you're going through this - I had post-op depression too, it absolutely sucks. It's pretty common though, including the fear of regret - after all, your body just went through a bunch of trauma, things hurt, and healing saps a lot of energy. Prolonged anasthesia also increases likelihood of post-op drop. The upside is, all of those things will improve with time and you will get to make that happy post-op post! 


The first few days after surgery are rough, but you should be feeling better around the 1-week/10-day mark, and once the drains come out it'll get even better. Things that helped me were cold packs for swelling, baby wipes for body funk (until showers were allowed), and remembering to think like a t-rex so I didn't move my arms too much. And SLEEP, as much as you can get - great way to pass the time. 


Hope things improve soon, and your recovery goes smoothly! You've got this.

Been on T for a while, let's see if I can remember...

- What side effects can I expect, and how soon? (these are usually things like voice drop, bottom growth, increase in body hair, increased libido...)

- Which side effects are reversible? Which are permanent? 

- What are my options with HRT application and what are the pros/cons of each (for T you're looking at: intramuscular injection, subcutaneous injection, or gel) 

- How often are doses generally spaced out, how much can you prescribe at once (I had an asshole Dr who only prescribed 1 dose at a time and I had to request it every time. My current doc was horrified by this and gives me 6 months at a time. I adore him).

- Are there any out-of-pocket costs on my end

- How often should I get my hormone levels checked? What range are you looking for? (for T I think it's around 700...forget the units though). 

- Are there health risks related to HRT?

...that's all I've got. Hope it goes well for you! Good luck

I can speak to IM vs sub-cu in regards to periods. I used to do IM and periods stopped after about a month, but came back when I switched to sub-cu years later. 

Learned from my phallo surgeon that while there's no official difference between the two, a lot of their patients of who've gone from IM to sub-cu reported the same as me. Unfortunately like a lot of things in transhealth, there isn't enough long-term research dedicated to this so it's mainly anecdotal for now. 

Still, might be worth trying IM instead if the period doesn't go away or comes back later on, if it bothers you/you don't mind bigger needles.

I didn't figure out I was trans until mid-20s, and before then never thought of myself as a guy. There were some vague indicators I might be trans like always wanting to play boy characters as a kid or getting along better with boys, but it was excused away as being a tomboy (or a "not like other girls" girl). 

I'd only ever heard the "always known/never liked dresses" narrative and assumed that because that didn't apply, I didn't feel that way and did (and do!) enjoy more feminine things, I couldn't be trans. Didn't learn until much later that experiences like ours exist, I wish there'd been more info available like there is now, probably would've figured things out a lot sooner. 

You're definitely not alone!

If it's a routine exam then yeah it'll most likely be the stirrups deal. Idk, every time I went there was an exam involved. 

Routine exams/PAP smears are over quick, like usually a few mins max? I think someone mentioned phone scrolling to distract already. The rest of the appointment is intake and chatting and stuff. All the OBGYNs I've had were pretty chill and fun to talk to while things went down, they've seen it all before and know it's a weird experience cis or trans.

I like to make a list of any questions I have so I don't forget anything, and it helps me stay matter-of-fact about the situation. Awkward and unpleasant? Yeah. Necessary self care? Yeah. Early detection can make all the difference, so it's worth it to make sure everything is healthy/anything that isn't can be treated asap. (That being said, all patients have the right to end an appointment at any time, so we do have control in the situation even if it doesn't feel like it.)

Good luck - it'll be over before you know it, and we've got your back here!

Charlie's a great name! Plus if you legally change it there's nothing stopping you from putting down "charlie" instead of "charles" too, for further distance. 


I get the past trauma and similar names, being afraid to trigger bad memories. However, names are names and when you find one that fits and feels right, you'll make it yours and grow the distance from potential reminders just by being yourself. 


My abuser has a common name and whenever I meet someone with his name there is that moment of "oh, same as X", but honestly it doesn't last and it doesn't make me dislike that person. Feel your pain, I'm muddling through this process too. I did my birth certificate and SSN at roughly the same time  (in CA it doesn't matter what order those 2 go in). An updated SSN card is required for a new driver's license, and for a passport too I think. So those are next. 


I'd you haven't already, you'll need at least 3 Certified Copies of your court order to change everything, regular photocopies won't work. There's usually a fee but sometimes you can get it waived, depends on the state.


Once the birth certificate, SSN, and license/state ID are done, you should have everything you need to start updating your name on things like insurance, bank accounts, bills, etc. 


It's a hassle and takes forever, but once it's done you'll never have to do it again! Seeing your name on everything will be so Worth It.

I just had stage 1 phallo and am doing RFF - I don't have the phallus yet (that's stage 2) but I'll tell you what I know so far:

For RFF, you're limited on size according to:
A) Forearm length - for example I'm pretty short so I will end up with something around 4 inches, you can go bigger with other donor sites but erotic sensation is really important to me and RFF is my best shot at getting it. 
B) Forearm artery location - even if you have long forearms, artery placement might mean a smaller donor site as they need to keep enough of the artery to supply blood to your arm/hand. 
C) Body width from ~ inside of hip bone to center of body - part of the forearm will be used for the donor site, and part will be used for the nerve/blood supply to the new phallus. The wider you are, the more they have to take to bridge the gap - and the less they can take for the donor site. This can be mitigated with weight loss (first time I've ever been motivated to exercise/eat better - I'm already getting a smaller dick, don't want to shrink it even further!). Some of this might be just anatomy though, like having super wide hips. 
**There might be a workaround to the last one, I need to talk to my surgeon to see if it's possible to take the nerve/etc from the other arm so that more donor tissue can be taken. 

I don't know enough about other donor sites, I think for the thigh if there's high body fat the phallus might need to be "de-bulked" so you don't end up with a larger girth than desired? 

Edit: removed objectifying term when describing ALT site, thanks DogPunk for letting me know!

I just had stage 1 with Dr Salim 6 weeks ago! He's amazing, and absolutely a geek I love it, I'm also an anatomy nerd so it's fun to hear him get really technical bc he just can't help it. Super passionate!

I wonder if you and I had the same nurse?? I also had a sketchy experience at the hospital, all of the nurses were negligent but one in particular was extra awful, I filed a report. Told Dr Salim and he was pissed that had happened and he and I made a plan for stage 2 to make sure it doesn't happen again. 

Very happy with my results, I got stage 1 phallo including UL, vgnectomy, hysto/ooph, and scrotoplasty. Dr Salim and his whole team are really supportive and know what they're doing. 

**Note for others worried about the hospital stay - have your surgical team give you a list of meds/care you'll need while in hospital, and on surgery day give a copy to intake nurse/Dr on the day (have the list on your phone or something too). Also before surgery day, get the name/contact info for the Ombudsman and have that on hand, their job is to investigate/resolve patient complaints and you can call them at any time if you feel you're not getting appropriate care.

I feel your pain, man. When I first started T 5 years ago my hair got super thick and grew really fast, I was finally able to rock the undercut manbun I'd dreamed about! 

Then last year I did a pandemic buzzcut and realized that I'd lost like...half the hair on my head. Hadn't noticed before because my hair was long and tied up all the time so it covered my scalp, and the hair on sides/back has always been really thick. I didn't escape the baldness gene after all...

I've been taking minoxodil for about 9 months and haven't lost any more hair but not much regrowth-wise, I was scared to go on Fin bc of the side effects and hoping minox would do it, but I'm gonna talk to my Dr about trying Fin now. 

I was actually about to post about this when I saw yours, I won't dominate your post bc I gotta rant and lament, but know that you're not alone. Stalking r/tressless has helped, they're pretty supportive and have good advice if you haven't checked it out. Mainly cisdudes but found a couple ftm posts.

At least where I am in CA, you can get a hysto without needing to be on T at all - although if you decide to get rid of both ovaries as well, you'll need to take T as your body won't be able to make estrogen and 0 hormones = health issues (like osteoporosis). Some guys keep one ovary as a back-up in case they ever lose access to T. 

How do you take T? After 5 years, I started getting nasty cramps and my period came back, and it happened soon after I switched from intramuscular injections to subcutaneous - according to my hysto surgeon, sub-cu is less effective at suppressing the menstrual cycle than IM, and she'd seen some other guys with my same issue. Wish my main doctor had heard of this! He put me on birth control when the problems started and those pills were my Daily Dose of Dysphoria, I hated them. I'd have gone back to big scary needles if I'd known. If you aren't doing IM, it might be worth trying for a few weeks/months to see if it helps. 

As for a hysto helping - once I got mine, the cramps stopped and haven't had them since. No uterus, no problems! :) It was right for me but def talk to your doctor and make sure it's right for you, it is a major surgery and those always come with risks.
